chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
"en": "Fast for the sighting of the crescent moon and break your fast for its sighting; and if two trustworthy witnesses testify before you that they have seen it, then complete it (the month)." }
Fast for the sighting of the crescent moon and break your fast for its sighting; and if two trustworthy witnesses testify before you that they have seen it, then complete it (the month).

key_terms.فَاقْضِهِ: Then complete it (referring to the month of fasting)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on determining the start and end of Ramadan based on moon sighting?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the foundational Shia jurisprudence of *ru'yah* (visual sighting) for Ramadan, emphasizing the authority of two just (*marji*) witnesses as sufficient proof. It highlights the practical legal mechanism where communal testimony overrides individual observation, ensuring unity in the start and end of the fasting month. This ruling underscores the Shia reliance on empirical evidence and the reliability of the *ahl al-hal wa'l-aqd* in religious observances.
